mentions.excerpt: Kris of Potential Multibaggers offers the strongest evidence that present demand is genuine.
On the question of demand today, Kris has the better evidence.

mentions.section: Long the chips, short the returns
mentions.excerpt: Kris makes the same concession from the other flank.
Kris of Potential Multibaggers saw the valuation problem before the listing.
In a June 8 warning, Kris wrote that retail buyers at the expected price would be paying out insiders and early investors at the top of the hype cycle.
Kris of Potential Multibaggers argues that the risk of investing too little is far greater than the risk of investing too much.
Kris, who writes Potential Multibaggers, adds a third-quarter growth estimate of 5.1% to inflation and gets nominal growth above 8%, comfortably above the Fed’s new rate.
Potential Multibaggers makes the arithmetic explicit.
Kris sees Amazon’s cloud unit unable to serve all its AI demand despite heavy orders for Nvidia chips and its own Trainium processors.
AWS has had more demand for AI capacity than it could supply, Kris of Potential Multibaggers says, despite large Nvidia orders and Amazon’s own chips.
Kris, on September 14, relayed Vercel's count: open models at 62% of its AI Gateway tokens, from 28.4% two months earlier.

sides.claim: The Google SpaceX GPU rental is bullish for Nvidia because there are still not enough GPUs to quench demand; Nvidia ramps production continuously but cannot follow demand.
Bullish on demand, and endorses the GFC earnings-quality parallel.
Retail buyers of the SpaceX IPO are the exit liquidity: the fancy name for paying insiders, VCs and early investors at peak hype valuations.
The Google SpaceX GPU rental is bullish for Nvidia because there are still not enough GPUs to quench demand; Nvidia ramps production continuously but cannot follow demand.

The Mag7 capex boom should be read the same way: the risk of not investing heavily is much higher than the risk of overinvesting, which is why Alphabet announced more investment and others will follow, since their existence is at stake.

The main reason for higher inflation is probably the more expensive oil, and a higher interest rate will not cure that; the Fed just wants to ensure inflation doesn't get out of hand.
